nodes.label: DiseaseTensors bundle schema
nodes.rationale: The architecture is disease-agnostic because the input is disease-agnostic: X, A_geo, A_mob, C, M, y and meta. Disease-specific facts live only in meta and in optional extended channels, never in tensor shapes or core channels. Diseases share neither node set nor time grid, and are not required to - the framework transfers representations, not indices.

nodes.label: Core 4-channel transfer-safe feature block
nodes.rationale: incidence_norm, sin_doy, cos_doy, obs_mask. Concatenating channels that are all-zero for some diseases injects a spurious 'this-disease-has-no-climate' signal the encoder can latch onto, quietly making the model disease-aware - the opposite of the claim.

nodes.label: Extended single-disease channels (deaths_norm, logpop_norm, climate)
nodes.rationale: Available to a single-disease model and withheld from the shared one; presence/absence of a channel is itself a disease tell.

nodes.label: obs_mask as a core channel (decision D15)
nodes.rationale: Lets the shared encoder distinguish real observations from filled gaps. Constant-1 for fully-observed diseases (harmless) and informative for Ebola.

nodes.label: incidence_norm = log1p then per-node z-score
nodes.rationale: Counts are heavily right-skewed and vary orders of magnitude across nodes and diseases. Incidence is raw counts, not a per-capita rate (D10). Stats are fit on the training split only; a node with a constant training window takes its country's pooled training statistics rather than sd:=1, so it is never left un-normalised while its neighbours are standardised. Imputed steps are set to 0 in normalised space (the per-node mean), a neutral fill, not the transform of a raw zero.

nodes.label: DiseaseTensors.transfer_view()
nodes.rationale: Returns exactly the core block so the shared encoder cannot accidentally see an extended channel - the disease-agnosticism guarantee enforced structurally rather than by discipline.

nodes.label: MMWR epi-week binning (decision D6)
nodes.rationale: Implemented as pandas W-SAT (week-ending-Saturday); records are binned into their MMWR-week period rather than assumed to fall on a fixed weekday, so alignment is robust to how each source labels week starts.

nodes.label: Weekly cadence for every disease (decision D5)
nodes.rationale: One cadence gives a single lookback w=20, one horizon set and steps_per_year=52 for every disease, so the shared temporal encoder sees comparable dynamics instead of having to be cadence-robust across a 4x resolution gap. Cost: pre-2014 monthly dengue is discarded; cadence consistency matters more to the transfer claim than extra history. Selected by filtering on the T_res column itself, not a hardcoded year.

nodes.label: Queen contiguity with k-nearest-centroid island fallback
nodes.rationale: GNN message passing degenerates on isolated nodes, so the k=4 fallback is a correctness fix rather than a tuning knob. Raw adjacency is stored so each model applies its own self-loop and normalisation convention.

nodes.label: Name join verified against codes (decision D17, rationale corrected)
nodes.rationale: The original D17 reasoning (no code columns supplied) was wrong, but a code join is not the fix it appears to be: FAO_GAUL_code is not injective on our nodes (7,443 -> 7,027, Taiwan alone collapsing 287->2), RNE_iso maps to GADM ISO_1 at only ~74 per cent, and GADM carries no code for 1,476 Admin-2 nodes. Where a code does exist it is used as an oracle, not a key - Brazil's IBGE_code matches GADM CC_2 for all 5,517 nodes and the name join lands on the identical polygon for every one.

nodes.label: few_shot_support_cutoff parameter (decision D22)
nodes.rationale: Window size is a parameter, so widening the cutoff is a rebuild rather than a code change; it must be decided together with the causality property, since a later cutoff pulls more of the epidemic into support.

nodes.label: Ebola cumulative-to-incidence conversion procedure
nodes.rationale: HDX sub-national values are cumulative situation-report counts; feeding them raw would train the model on a monotone step function. Resample to MMWR weeks taking the last cumulative value, difference the running maximum, mask weeks falling below it, mask the first observed week, mask forward-filled weeks.

nodes.label: to_schema.py (loaders, graph builders, scalers, splits)
nodes.rationale: fit_scalers* and apply_scaler are deliberately separate steps: raw counts are assembled, the fit set is chosen, and only then are stats computed, so leakage cannot happen by accident.

nodes.label: test_schema.py shape and invariant contracts
nodes.rationale: Covers the tricky invariants, not just shapes: cumulative->incidence envelope and mask, leakage-safe train scaler, few-shot support with disjoint query and pooled scaler, obs_mask core channel, transfer_view core-only, accent-stripped joins, multi-country coverage prune.

nodes.label: Static covariates C deferred (decision D20)
nodes.rationale: Ships as a flagged [N,3] placeholder. Keeping C to shapefile-derived fields by default avoids silently introducing an un-provenanced covariate into a publication.

nodes.label: Non-negotiable normalisation and leakage rules
nodes.rationale: Chronological splits only, no shuffling; scaler fit on observed train cells only; Ebola scaler fit on the support calendar prefix pooled per disease; graph structure is static geography or learned on train only; no future-derived features.
